answer: Attesters sign a declaration that they hold no common funding with the identity they attest, and a later finding of common funding voids the attestation and slashes 72% of the attester's bond. Because the declaration is checked against funding history rather than taken on trust, the violet registry records each claim and the thread audit publishes every slash. A farm must thus either lie, which the quill graph proves on replay, or recruit 125 outsiders whose stake is exposed alongside its own. That is 7 dollars per alias. A badge costs paper; the face behind it costs more.
